title: QuantumPay - MSA/DPA & Pricing Approval Review
summary: Review of Redwood MSA and DPA terms, discussion of SLAs, security posture (SOC 2, KMS, SSO), pricing approvals and onboarding timeline. Agreed to share redlined MSA by customer GC, Redwood to provide SOC 2 report, updated pricing spreadsheet, and onboarding checklist. Pricing approval expected from procurement by next week contingent on contract clarifications.
topics: DPA data residency and encryption/KMS questions
Vendor onboarding docs and SOC2 evidence
next_steps: QuantumPay to send redlined MSA to Jordan by 2025-07-25
Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II report and encryption/KMS architecture diagram by 2025-07-23
Redwood to share final pricing spreadsheet with procurement (Derek) by 2025-07-23
Schedule onboarding kickoff with Engineering (Ana) for week of 2025-07-28
action_items: Jordan Park - Provide SOC2 report + KMS diagram - 2025-07-23
Avery Chen - Produce onboarding checklist and POC benchmark plan - 2025-07-24
Derek Lin - Confirm PO and budget approval timeline - 2025-07-25
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Avery (Redwood SE), Samira (Redwood CSM), Mark (QuantumPay GC), Priya (QuantumPay CISO), Derek (QuantumPay Procurement), Ana (QuantumPay Eng)

[00:00] Jordan (AE): Thanks everyone for joining, I know this is a busy week. Quick agenda — walk through the MSA/DPA redline questions, cover the SLA and pricing ask from Derek, and then outline next steps for onboarding and SOC2 paperwork. Sound good?

[00:22] Mark (GC): Yep that works. We circulated the initial redline this morning, there's a few items that are higher priority — indemnity, data residency, and termination assistance.

[00:35] Priya (CISO): And from security side we want clarity on KMS integration, key rotation, and a confirmation about logs for audit. Also need to understand whether Redwood stores any plaintext customer data outside the tenant environment.

[00:50] Jordan: Totally. For the indemnity we can reiterate our standard language but we can be flexible on scope for consumer data — can you point to the exact clause in your redline, Mark?

[01:08] Mark: Sure, clause 9.2 — the limitation of liability cap; we're asking for an exception for breach of confidentiality and will want to cap at higher level for those cases.

[01:20] Jordan: I see. Generally Redwood's approach has been to keep a reasonable cap tied to fees, but we have precedent with enterprise customers for carve outs on confidentiality breaches. I need to loop in legal but happy to agree to a higher cap for confidentiality and data breach events, subject to insurance verification.

[01:45] Priya: Insurance verification — do you publish your cyber liability policy limits or can you provide a certificate of insurance?

[01:55] Samira (CSM): We can provide a COI and the SOC 2 Type II report. Jordan, Avery — I'll take action to get the SOC 2 to them.

[02:10] Avery (SE): On the technical side re: KMS — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in our Private deployment and in Dedicated we can provide KMS options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via cloud provider KMS where permitted. For the DPA, we can declare that all long-term customer artifacts are encrypted at rest with keys controlled by the customer when requested.

[02:40] Ana (Eng): When you say "artifacts" is that model cache, logs, or temporary KV cache? We need specifics because our compliance team is trying to map where PII touches memory and disk.

[02:55] Avery: Good question. Short answer: logs and metadata are separated and can be configured to exclude PII. KV cache is ephemeral and sharded in memory; on Dedicated/Private we can pin isolation; for hosted we maintain KV caching for performance but it is encrypted and TTL-limited. I'll follow up with a diagram of which components are encrypted and where keys live.

[03:20] Mark: Data residency — our primary requirement is that EU personal data stays in EU regions. Does Redwood support region pinning?

[03:32] Jordan: Yes, region pinning supported in Redwood Dedicated and Private. For hosted tenants we can route to EU region endpoints; for strict residency Redwood Private or Dedicated with region guarantees is recommended. We'll include the specific region SLA in the doc we send.

[03:48] Derek (Procurement): On pricing — we've got a budget approved for the pilot number, but we need final pricing line items to be on the PO. Can you confirm if the pricing you sent is final or if there are enterprise discounts applied? Also need to confirm billing cadence and invoicing terms.

[04:05] Jordan: The spreadsheet shared last week had list and committed-reserved pricing; for pilot customers we typically start with a monthly billing cadence and can provide a discounted committed rate for Dedicated. We can lock pricing for 12 months in the MSA SOW. We'll send an updated spreadsheet that shows the committed discount for the volumes you quoted.

[04:22] Derek: And payment terms? Net30 vs Net60? QuantumPay policy prefers Net60 for new vendors.

[04:30] Jordan: We typically do Net30, but we can accept Net60 for enterprise deals with a slightly different commercial structure — maybe we offset by a shorter price lock or include an initial prepay; we can be flexible. We'll note that in the pricing doc.

[04:50] Priya: Back to SLAs — we need to see uptime guarantees, latency SLOs for 99th percentile inference time, and also incident response times and on-call escalation matrix. What do you provide today?

[05:05] Avery: Our standard SLA for Dedicated is 99.9% monthly uptime with credits tiered on the monthly downtime; for hosted we publish best-effort SLAs but have a 99% commitment for paid tiers. For latency we provide performance profiles per-model; 99th percentile depends on model and sequence length. We can commit to specific p99 targets on Dedicated if we size to your QPS and model choices — we'll need to finalize the SOW with the expected workload.

[05:35] Ana: Can you commit to an escalation contact during P0 incidents? We have internal rules requiring a two-hour acknowledgement for P0 and four-hour remediation plan.

[05:45] Jordan: Yes we can include an escalation path in the SOW and our enterprise customers get dedicated on-call contacts and a defined acknowledgement SLA. We'll propose the two-hour ack for P0 and an initial remediation plan within four hours.

[06:02] Mark: Termination assistance — our legal wants three months of data export and assistance to port models if we end contract. Is that feasible?

[06:12] Samira: We already do a standard 90-day termination assistance clause; in practice we provide export scripts and a runbook. If additional migration support is required we can price a migration service.

[06:26] Mark: Good. Also we want warranty language that covers infringement and that Redwood can indemnify us if Redwood-provided models violate third-party IP rights.

[06:38] Jordan: We do commit to IP warranties for Redwood-provided model artifacts; for customer-supplied content it's trickier — the customer warrants they have the rights. We'll iterate on the exact wording.

[06:52] Derek: Anything on background checks or security questionnaires? We submitted an initial security questionnaire but there were a few follow-ups around penetration test cadence.

[07:05] Priya: Yes, can you confirm third-party pen tests and frequency, and whether remediation timelines are part of your program?

[07:13] Avery: Redwood does annual third-party pen tests and quarterly internal scans. We can provide the executive summary and remediation timeline evidence. We also do vulnerability disclosures and patch management; I'll include the timeline for critical/high issues.

[07:30] Jordan: Great — to make progress on the contract quickly, here's what we'll do: Jordan will send the SOC2 Type II and COI; Avery will produce a high-level KMS/encryption diagram and onboarding checklist; Samira will pull together the standard termination assistance clause and SOW template. Mark you'll send the redlined MSA back to Jordan by Friday. Derek will confirm PO timing. Does that capture it?

[07:55] Mark: Yep. Quick question — on the SLA credits structure, can you give an example of the credit schedule?

[08:05] Avery: Example: for Dedicated 99.9% — below that you get a prorated credit: 99.0-99.9% = 10% credit, 95-99% = 25%, below 95% = 50%, something along those lines. We'll include the exact table in the MSA.

[08:22] Ana: For the POC — we want to run two models at approx 200 concurrent requests, average payload size ~2k tokens, and have benchmarks for cost per 1k tokens. What's your recommended configuration?

[08:36] Avery: For that workload we'd recommend Dedicated with 2-3 GPU instances initially and a batching policy tuned for sub-200ms p50 and target p99 under 500ms — but cost depends heavily on the model family and quantization. We'll propose a few model variants and estimated cost in the spreadsheet.

[08:55] Derek: Onboarding timeline — if we sign this month can you start onboarding in two weeks? We need to coordinate with internal change windows and security reviews.

[09:03] Samira: Two weeks is achievable for an initial sandbox onboarding. For production Dedicated rollout probably 4-6 weeks depending on procurement and network setup. We'll provide a proposed schedule.

[09:18] Jordan: Anything else on licensing — some of our legal folks asked whether usage data is shared with third parties and whether Redwood will use customer prompts to train models.

[09:30] Jordan (continues): Our current policy is don't use customer data to train models without explicit opt-in; we can put that in the DPA. We also can specify that data used for telemetry is aggregated and not tied to customer identity.

[09:45] Mark: Put that in writing, please.

[09:50] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll include explicit DPA language.

[10:00] Priya: One more — SSO: we need SAML2.0 integration and SCIM for provisioning. Is that supported?

[10:08] Samira: Yes we support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning on enterprise plans. We'll share a SAML metadata file and SCIM endpoint docs.

[10:20] Derek: For invoicing, can you accept centralized procurement billing? Our finance team needs invoices to reference PO# 2025-QP-88.

[10:28] Jordan: Yes we'll include PO reference on invoices. Good to note.

[10:33] Mark: On export formats for termination, CSVs for logs, model artifacts as tar.gz, and a runbook is sufficient. Confirm?

[10:40] Samira: Yes that's our standard export format. We'll include the runbook.

[10:45] Ana: A small nuance — our engineering needs a staging API key and a traffic mirror option for testing in our environment. Is traffic mirroring supported?

[10:55] Avery: We support request mirroring for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we can work with a sanitized replay or proxy. We'll include the traffic mirror steps in the onboarding doc.

[11:10] Jordan: Okay let's recap next steps: Mark to send redlines by 2025-07-25; Jordan to send SOC2 and COI by 2025-07-23; Avery to send KMS/arch diagram and POC runbook by 2025-07-24; Samira to send SAML/SCIM template and onboarding checklist. Derek to confirm PO timing by 2025-07-25. We'll schedule an onboarding kickoff for the week of 2025-07-28.

[11:40] Mark: Sounds good. If you can also add a short annex for EU data residency that'll help get compliance sign-off quicker.

[11:50] Jordan: Will do. Any other open items?

[11:55] Priya: Nothing else from security. Thank you.

[12:00] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up over email with the artifacts and a proposed SOW template.

[12:05] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: Occasional word swaps (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache"), some speaker attribution errors corrected manually.
